items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2023 OD Standard
items.stem: Prove that √2 is an irrational number.
items.answer:
Assume that √2 is a rational number. Then it can be written as √2 = p/q, where p and q are co-prime integers and q ≠ 0.
So p = q√2.
Squaring both sides, p² = 2q².
Thus 2 is a factor of p², and hence 2 is a factor of p.
Let p = 2c, where c is some integer. Then p² = 4c².
Substituting p² = 2q², we get 2q² = 4c², i.e. q² = 2c².
Thus 2 is a factor of q², and hence 2 is a factor of q.
So 2 is a common factor of p and q, which contradicts the fact that p and q are co-prime.
Hence our assumption is wrong, and √2 is an irrational number.

items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2024 OD Standard
items.stem: In a teachers' workshop, the number of teachers teaching French, Hindi and English are 48, 80 and 144 respectively. Find the minimum number of rooms required if in each room the same number of teachers are seated and all of them are of the same subject.
items.answer:
The number of rooms will be minimum if every room has the maximum number of participants, so the number of teachers in each room must be the HCF of 48, 80 and 144.
48 = 2⁴ × 3
80 = 2⁴ × 5
144 = 2⁴ × 3²
HCF(48, 80, 144) = 2⁴ = 16, so 16 teachers can be seated in each room.
Minimum number of rooms = (48 + 80 + 144)/16 = 272/16 = 17.
Thus the minimum number of rooms required is 17.

items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | Board 2020 SQP Standard
items.stem: Given that √5 is irrational, prove that 2√5 − 3 is an irrational number.
items.answer:
Assume that 2√5 − 3 is a rational number. Then it can be written as 2√5 − 3 = p/q, where p and q are co-prime integers and q ≠ 0.
Rewriting, 2√5 = p/q + 3, so √5 = (p + 3q)/(2q).
Here (p + 3q)/(2q) is rational because p and q are integers, so √5 would have to be a rational number.
But this contradicts the given fact that √5 is irrational.
Hence 2√5 − 3 is an irrational number.

items.stem: Given that √3 is irrational, prove that 2√3 − 5 is an irrational number.
items.answer:
Assume that 2√3 − 5 is a rational number, so 2√3 − 5 = p/q where p and q are co-prime integers and q ≠ 0.
Then 2√3 = p/q + 5, so √3 = (p + 5q)/(2q).
The right-hand side is rational, so √3 would be rational, which contradicts the given fact that √3 is irrational.
Hence 2√3 − 5 is an irrational number.

items.stem: Given that √2 is irrational, prove that (5 + 3√2) is an irrational number.
items.answer:
Assume that (5 + 3√2) is a rational number. Then it can be written as 5 + 3√2 = p/q, where p and q are co-prime integers and q ≠ 0.
Rewriting, 3√2 = p/q − 5, so √2 = (p − 5q)/(3q).
Here (p − 5q)/(3q) is rational because p and q are integers, so √2 would have to be a rational number.
But this contradicts the given fact that √2 is irrational.
Hence (5 + 3√2) is an irrational number.

items.stem: Prove that 2 + 5√3 is an irrational number, given that √3 is an irrational number.
items.answer:
Assume that 2 + 5√3 is a rational number, so 2 + 5√3 = p/q where p and q are co-prime integers and q ≠ 0.
Then 5√3 = p/q − 2 = (p − 2q)/q, so √3 = (p − 2q)/(5q).
The right-hand side is rational, so √3 would be rational, which contradicts the given fact that √3 is irrational.
Hence 2 + 5√3 is an irrational number.

items.stem: Prove that (2 + √3)/5 is an irrational number, given that √3 is an irrational number.
items.answer:
Assume that (2 + √3)/5 is a rational number, so (2 + √3)/5 = p/q where p and q are co-prime integers and q ≠ 0.
Then 2 + √3 = 5p/q, so √3 = 5p/q − 2 = (5p − 2q)/q.
The right-hand side is rational, so √3 would be rational, which contradicts the given fact that √3 is irrational.
Hence (2 + √3)/5 is an irrational number.

items.stem: Write the smallest number which is divisible by both 306 and 657.
items.answer:
The smallest number that is divisible by two numbers is obtained by finding the LCM of those numbers.
306 = 6 × 51 = 3 × 2 × 3 × 17 = 2 × 3² × 17
657 = 9 × 73 = 3 × 3 × 73 = 3² × 73
LCM(306, 657) = 2 × 3 × 3 × 17 × 73 = 22338
Hence the smallest number which is divisible by both 306 and 657 is 22338.

items.stem: 144 cartons of Coke cans and 90 cartons of Pepsi cans are to be stacked in a canteen. If each stack is of the same height and if it is to contain cartons of the same drink, what would be the greatest number of cartons each stack would have?
items.answer:
The required answer is the HCF of 144 and 90.
144 = 2⁴ × 3²
90 = 2 × 3² × 5
HCF(144, 90) = 2 × 3² = 18
Thus each stack would have 18 cartons.

items.stem: Three bells toll at intervals of 9, 12, 15 minutes respectively. If they start tolling together, after what time will they next toll together?
items.answer:
The required answer is the LCM of 9, 12 and 15 minutes. Finding the prime factors of the given numbers,
9 = 3 × 3 = 3²
12 = 2 × 2 × 3 = 2² × 3
15 = 3 × 5
LCM(9, 12, 15) = 2² × 3² × 5 = 180 minutes
The bells will toll next together after 180 minutes, i.e. after 3 hours.

items.stem: Find HCF and LCM of 16 and 36 by prime factorization and check your answer.
items.answer:
Finding the prime factors of the given numbers,
16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁴
36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 2² × 3²
HCF(16, 36) = 2 × 2 = 4
LCM(16, 36) = 2⁴ × 3² = 16 × 9 = 144
Check: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
4 × 144 = 16 × 36
576 = 576
Thus LHS = RHS.

items.section_heading: THREE MARKS QUESTIONS | PRACTICE | Board Term-1 2011
items.stem: Find the HCF and LCM of 510 and 92 and verify that HCF × LCM = Product of two given numbers.
items.answer:
510 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 17 and 92 = 2² × 23.
HCF(510, 92) = 2
LCM(510, 92) = 2² × 3 × 5 × 17 × 23 = 23460
Verification: HCF × LCM = 2 × 23460 = 46920 and 510 × 92 = 46920, so HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
Hence HCF = 2 and LCM = 23460.

items.stem: Find HCF and LCM of 404 and 96 and verify that HCF × LCM = Product of the two given numbers.
items.answer:
404 = 2² × 101 and 96 = 2⁵ × 3.
HCF(404, 96) = 2² = 4
LCM(404, 96) = 2⁵ × 3 × 101 = 9696
Verification: HCF × LCM = 4 × 9696 = 38784 and 404 × 96 = 38784, so HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
Hence HCF = 4 and LCM = 9696.

items.stem: The length, breadth and height of a room are 8 m 50 cm, 6 m 25 cm and 4 m 75 cm respectively. Find the length of the longest rod that can measure the dimensions of the room exactly.
items.answer:
Here we have to determine the HCF of all the lengths, since that is the largest measure which can measure every dimension exactly.
Length l = 8 m 50 cm = 850 cm = 50 × 17 = 2 × 5² × 17
Breadth b = 6 m 25 cm = 625 cm = 25 × 25 = 5⁴
Height h = 4 m 75 cm = 475 cm = 25 × 19 = 5² × 19
HCF(l, b, h) = HCF(850, 625, 475) = HCF(2 × 5² × 17, 5⁴, 5² × 19) = 5² = 25 cm
Thus a rod of 25 cm can measure the dimensions of the room exactly, and it is the longest such rod.
